section: Satavahanas - origin debate, Simuka, Gautamiputra Satakarni, Nasik Prasasti, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi
subsections: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni
Nasik Prasasti - issuer, reign, language, titles

accepted.s: Which ruler is placed sixth in the dynastic sequence of the Satavahanas?
accepted.x: Satakarni II is identified as the sixth ruler in the Satavahana dynastic sequence.
accepted.tq: Use the dynastic position as the decisive clue rather than the ruler’s achievement.

accepted.s: Who is regarded as the greatest of the later Satavahana rulers?
accepted.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni is described as the greatest of the later Satavahana rulers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish between the greatest early ruler and the greatest later ruler.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Hala is placed as the seventeenth ruler. Yajna Sri Satakarni, Gautamiputra Satakarni and Pulumavi III are placed as the twenty-seventh, twenty-third and thirtieth rulers respectively.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical position of each ruler before accepting the pair.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Satavahana rulers:
1. Satakarni II had the longest reign among the rulers listed.
2. His reign lasted for 56 years.
3. He is associated with the Sanchi torana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Satakarni II was the sixth ruler, reigned for 56 years—the longest reign in the listed sequence—and is associated with the Sanchi torana.
accepted.tq: Combine the ruler’s position, numerical detail and contribution before selecting the code.

accepted.s: The title ‘Kavivatsala’ is associated with which Satavahana ruler?
accepted.x: Hala, the seventeenth Satavahana ruler, bore the title ‘Kavivatsala’.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive title with the ruler, avoiding confusion with territorial titles.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: ‘Trisamudradhipati’ is associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni, not Hala. Hala bore the title ‘Kavivatsala’.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped ruler-title pair among otherwise correctly matched titles.

accepted.s: Which one of the following titles was associated with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi?
accepted.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi bore the titles ‘Dakshinapatheshwara’ and ‘Navanagaraswami’.
accepted.tq: Separate Pulumavi’s titles from those of Satakarni I, Hala and Yajna Sri.

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the title ‘Trisamudradhipati’ in the tradition attributed to Banabhatta?
accepted.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni is associated with the title ‘Trisamudradhipati’ in the Banabhatta tradition.
accepted.tq: Use the title as a direct identification clue and distinguish it from ‘Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana’.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following dynasties in the chronological order of their succession in Magadha:
A. Kanvas
B. Mauryas
C. Satavahanas
D. Sungas
accepted.x: The sequence is Mauryas, Sungas, Kanvas and then Satavahanas. Simuka is associated with the overthrow of the Kanvas.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last dynasties, then arrange the intervening succession.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the successors of the Satavahanas:
1. The Ikshvakus succeeded them in Andhra.
2. The Abhiras succeeded them in Maharashtra.
3. The Vakatakas succeeded them in Vidarbha.
4. The Pallavas were among their successors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The listed successors include the Ikshvakus in Andhra, Abhiras in Maharashtra, Vakatakas in Vidarbha and Pallavas. Chutus are also included among the successors.
accepted.tq: Treat each geographical succession as an independent statement before choosing the complete code.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct order of later political powers mentioned in connection with the succession after the Satavahanas?
accepted.x: After the Vakatakas and other immediate successors, the later sequence mentioned is Chalukyas followed by Rashtrakutas.
accepted.tq: Separate immediate successors from the later powers in the sequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Gautamiputra Satakarni is correct?
o: He defeated Nahapana and recovered territories including Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik.
He was the last great ruler of the Satavahana dynasty.
He belonged to the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas.
He founded the Kshaharata branch and issued the earliest Nasik inscription.
accepted.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana and recovered Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik. Nahapana belonged to the Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–enemy–territory relationship and reject swapped identities.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Nahapana, defeated by Gautamiputra Satakarni, belonged to which branch?
o: Karddamaka branch of the Western Kshatrapas
Satavahana branch of the Andhra rulers
Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas
Chutu branch of the Deccan rulers
accepted.x: Nahapana was a Western Kshatrapa of the Kshaharata branch.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two branches by linking Nahapana specifically with Kshaharata.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The restriking of whose silver coins by Gautamiputra Satakarni is evidenced by the Jogalthambi hoard?
accepted.x: The Jogalthambi hoard contains Nahapana’s silver coins restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni, providing evidence of Gautamiputra’s victory.
accepted.tq: Use the hoard as archaeological evidence for the ruler defeated and the victor’s action.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ushavadata, also known as Rishabhadatta, was the son-in-law of Nahapana. Ayama was Nahapana’s minister.
accepted.tq: Watch for the APPSC person-and-role swap between Ushavadata and Ayama.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ushavadata invested 2,000 karshapanas in which institution at Govardhana?
accepted.x: Ushavadata invested 2,000 karshapanas in a weavers’ guild at Govardhana.
accepted.tq: Link the precise amount with the economic institution rather than the donor’s family relationship.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with ship-motif coins and the extension of Satavahana rule into coastal Andhra?
accepted.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi issued ship-motif coins and extended Satavahana rule into coastal Andhra.
accepted.tq: Connect the coin motif with the ruler’s maritime and coastal expansion.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni?
1. Revival of maritime power
2. Ship coins
3. Patronage of Nagarjuna
4. Association with the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni is associated with the revival of maritime power, ship coins, patronage of Nagarjuna and the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara.
accepted.tq: Recognise the cluster of maritime, religious and architectural associations of one ruler.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Periplus refers to which aspect of the history of the Satavahanas?
o: The Kanva conquest of the Deccan
The foundation of the Nagarjunakonda Mahavihara
accepted.x: The Periplus notes the conflict between the Sakas and the Satavahanas.
accepted.tq: Match the literary source with the specific historical relationship it records.
accepted.sec: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, Sri Yajna Satakarni  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following literary works is NOT included among the traditions concerning the origins of the Satavahanas?
accepted.x: The Gathasaptasati does not narrate the early history of the Satavahanas. Traditions on their origins occur in the Kathasaritsagara, Dvatrimsatputtalika and Pratishthanapura Kalpa, among others.
accepted.tq: Find the work specifically excluded from the origin traditions.

accepted.s: Who wrote the Brihatkatha, which is mentioned in connection with Satavahana literary traditions?
accepted.x: The Brihatkatha is attributed to Gunadhya and was written in Paisachi.
accepted.tq: Match the literary work with its author and avoid confusing it with later retellings.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Katantra is associated with Sharvavarman and Kundala Satakarni. Leelavati Parinayam is associated with Kutuhala, while Brihatkatha is associated with Gunadhya.
accepted.tq: Use the three-part literary association—work, author and Satavahana connection—to eliminate swaps.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the literary traditions of Satavahana origins is correct?
1. Somadeva is associated with the Kathasaritsagara.
2. Jain traditions and the Dipavamsa also contain traditions relating to Satavahana origins.
3. The Gathasaptasati is the principal source for the early history of the dynasty.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Somadeva is associated with the Kathasaritsagara, and Jain and Dipavamsa traditions also discuss the origins. The Gathasaptasati does not narrate the early Satavahana history.
accepted.tq: Identify the single false source claim and retain the two supported literary traditions.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the chronology of the Satavahanas is correct?
o: The chronology contains no difference between Puranic and modern scholarly placements.
The dynasty is universally placed only between the fourth and fifth centuries CE.
The Puranic long chronology places Simuka approximately in 230–207 BCE.
The Puranic chronology places Simuka exclusively in the second century CE.
accepted.x: The Puranic long chronology places Simuka approximately in 230–207 BCE, while another chronology places the dynasty broadly from the first century BCE to the third century CE.
accepted.tq: Compare the two chronological frameworks instead of treating one disputed date as universal.

accepted.s: The chronology that places the Satavahana dynasty broadly between the first century BCE and the third century CE is associated in the material with which designation?
accepted.x: The CDI chronology places the Satavahana dynasty broadly in the period from the first century BCE to the third century CE.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a chronological designation from literary and travel sources.

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the Ashvamedha sacrifice, expansion into Central India and the issue of the first silver coins among the rulers listed?
accepted.x: Satakarni I is associated with the Ashvamedha, expansion into Central India and the first silver coins among the listed Satavahana rulers.
accepted.tq: Combine three distinctive achievements to identify the correct early ruler.

accepted.s: Satakarni I was a contemporary of which ruler?
accepted.x: Satakarni I is identified as a contemporary of Kharavela.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler to the contemporary from the same broad historical period.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Nasik Prasasti is correct?
1. It was composed in Prakrit prose.
2. It was written in the Brahmi script.
3. It records the expeditions, victories, empire and titles of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
4. It praises him as the destroyer of Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Nasik Prasasti is in Prakrit prose and Brahmi script and records Gautamiputra’s expeditions, victories, empire and titles, including his destruction of Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.
accepted.tq: Treat language, script, contents and titulature as four separate inscriptional clues.
accepted.sec: Nasik Prasasti - issuer, reign, language, titles  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Nasik Prasasti records gifts made by Gautami Balasri together with her son to monks on which hill?
accepted.x: The Nasik Prasasti records gifts made by Gautami Balasri and her son to monks on the Trirashmi hill.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific religious site linked with the recorded donation.
accepted.sec: Nasik Prasasti - issuer, reign, language, titles  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the Nasik Prasasti, Gautami Balasri is described as the wife of a:
accepted.x: Gautami Balasri is described in the Nasik Prasasti as the wife of a Rajarshi.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise honorific relationship used for the issuer’s status.
accepted.sec: Nasik Prasasti - issuer, reign, language, titles  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies Vasishthiputra Pulumavi in relation to the Satavahana sequence and inscriptions?
o: He was the twenty-fourth ruler and is associated with the Amaravati inscription.
He was the sixth ruler and commissioned the Sanchi torana.
He was the twenty-seventh ruler and issued the first Nasik inscription.
He was the thirtieth ruler and ended the Satavahana dynasty.
accepted.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi is placed as the twenty-fourth ruler and is associated with the Amaravati inscription. The twenty-seventh and thirtieth positions belong to Yajna Sri Satakarni and Pulomavi III respectively.
accepted.tq: Combine dynastic position with inscriptional association to avoid ruler-number swaps.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Yajna Sri Satakarni — patronage of Nagarjuna
Vasishthiputra Satakarni — marriage with Rudradaman’s daughter
Pulumavi III — revival of maritime power through ship coins
accepted.x: Pulumavi III is identified as the last ruler in the Puranic sequence, whereas revival of maritime power and ship coins are associated with Yajna Sri Satakarni.
accepted.tq: Find the contribution shifted from the last ruler to the last great ruler.
